evidence: app/app — zero tests, so zero noise, but also zero signal
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no low-value padding, per the rubric's neutral score for the empty case.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure whatsoever: no runner, no test script, no test files, despite the app containing substantial pure logic (loaders, comparators, formatters) that is straightforward to unit-test.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (plus @testing-library/react for the sort toggle and filter form) and a `test` script; loaders are async functions of fetch and can be tested with a stubbed fetch or a small API fixture.

findings.issue: The home loader's filter composition (search substring on humanized names, type via typesById, generation membership), page clamping and slice are untested; a data-layer refactor could introduce off-by-one pagination or broken filter conjunctions with nothing failing.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the loader against a small fixture species/type/generation set: combined filters, empty results, page beyond range clamps to pageCount, count matches across pages.

findings.issue: The sorting comparator implements the spec's subtlest rule (missing values last in both directions, name tie-break, mixed numeric/string columns) and has no regression guard; flipping null handling to nulls-first on descending would pass unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Extract/keep sortRows pure (it already is) and test each column in both directions including null power/accuracy cells.

findings.issue: URL-state machinery is untested: queryFor's omit-empty/omit-page-1 rules and the lastPushed-ref dance between debounced search input and navigate() — the latter is exactly where a refactor introduces stale-URL or lost-keystroke bugs.
findings.suggestion: Test queryFor directly (pure function) and add a component test for type-select change resetting page and search debounce pushing a replace entry.

findings.issue: cardsFromPokemon enforces alternate-form exclusion (id > 10000), dedupe and dex ordering for type/ability/move pages; removing the dedupe or the ID cutoff would show Mega forms and duplicates with no failing test.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with refs including IDs above 10000 and duplicates, asserting count, order and species (not form) names.

findings.issue: The promise cache's failure-eviction and 404-to-data(null,{status:404}) mapping are untested; a refactor could cache rejected promises or stop converting API 404s into route 404s, breaking every not-found URL at once.
findings.suggestion: Test getJson/getRecord with a stubbed fetch: 404 throws the route-not-found data, 500 does not get cached (second call retries), and an in-flight 404 promise is evicted.

findings.issue: Move grouping logic is untested: default game must be the highest-order group, the dedupe key move|method|level could collapse legitimate duplicate rows or admit duplicates, and METHOD_ORDER-then-alphabetical method ordering has no guard.
findings.suggestion: Test the grouping with a synthetic pokemon payload covering two version groups, an unknown method, and a move learned at two levels in the same group.

findings.issue: Only the 404 error path is exercised by acceptance tests; the generic error path (API 500/outage) and the meta title under error are untested.
findings.suggestion: A component test rendering ErrorBoundary with a non-404 error asserting the 'Something went wrong' heading and Back link.

findings.issue: Localization helpers (latest English flavor text must be the *last* en entry with whitespace collapsed; englishName fallback) are untested; changing find/find-last semantics would silently alter every description.
findings.suggestion: Plain unit tests over the existing local entry types, including entries with \n and \f runs.

findings.issue: Pure formatters (humanize, dexNumber, idFromUrl, orDash) — including spec-critical edges like `mr-mime` → `Mr Mime` vs the English name `Mr. Mime` — have no tests.
findings.suggestion: A handful of trivial vitest cases; cheapest insurance in the codebase.

summary: The app ships no tests of its own: no runner, no test script, zero test files. Since most risky logic lives in pure functions (loaders, sort comparators, URL-state builders, formatters), coverage would have been cheap to add and is now absent precisely where refactors will hurt. Once the external acceptance suite is no longer the guard, a broken filter conjunction, pagination off-by-one, nulls-first sort or cached 404 would ship unnoticed.
